chunks: Ibn Udhaynah narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If he gives her the choice or places her affair in her hand outside the period before her ʿiddah, without having two witnesses testify, then it is nothing. And if he gives her the choice or places her affair in her hand with the testimony of two witnesses in the period before her ʿiddah, then she has the choice so long as they have not separated. فإذا she chooses herself, then it is one divorce, and he has the greater right to take her back; and if she chooses her husband, then it is not a divorce.

key_terms.أَمْرَهَا بِيَدِهَا: he placed the matter in her own hand or authority
key_terms.بِٱلْخِيَارِ: having the option or legal choice
key_terms.خَيَّرَهَا: he gave her the choice regarding remaining or separating
key_terms.رَجْعَتِهَا: taking her back during a revocable divorce
key_terms.شَاهِدَيْنِ: two witnesses whose testimony is required for validity
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: her waiting period relevant to divorce rulings

ai.seo_question: When does giving a wife the choice of separation count as a valid divorce in Shia law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a husband giving his wife the choice or placing the matter in her hand regarding separation. It states that this only has legal effect when done with the testimony of two witnesses and within the proper legal time, and if she chooses separation it counts as one revocable divorce.
